title: Missed nursing care and shift-level staffing on 18 adult inpatient units
subtitle: Cross-sectional last-shift survey linked to unit staffing and acuity
statement: Nurses report that care is left undone on busy shifts, but the hospital has no measure of how often, of which activities, or whether missed care rises when a unit runs below planned staffing once patient acuity is considered. Management and the union both want figures they can trust. A last-shift survey of nurses linked to the scheduling and acuity records of the shift each nurse describes would answer this at one point in time.
whoAffected: Adult inpatients on 18 units, especially dependent older patients who need turning, mouth care and help to walk; about 1,150 registered and licensed practical nurses; unit managers and the budget committee.
whatHurts: Missed turning and mobilisation lead to pressure injuries and deconditioning, missed teaching leaves patients unprepared for discharge, and late timed medicines can cause harm. Nurses describe moral distress when they cannot finish care.
currentPractice: No routine measure of missed care. Staffing is planned by a core schedule and adjusted daily; acuity scores are entered each morning but not linked to any outcome.
whyNow: The next budget round, conflicting claims from management and the union, and an REB approval and union agreement already in place.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients on every unit receive essential nursing care on every shift, and staffing decisions rest on evidence that nurses and managers both accept.
summary: Problem framed as a cross-sectional survey question on missed care and shift-level staffing, with acuity as the key competing explanation.
